semantic_reconciliation.finding: Retrieval admission already persists retrieval_id, turn_id, episode_id, causal_id, session_id, generation and query_hash; the identity substrate is present upstream.
Each UserPromptSubmit creates fresh round-scoped causal_id, turn_id and episode_id and passes them into retrieval, so distinct same-session rounds are intentionally representable.
Stop relevance receives session/transcript context, chooses the newest same-session unjudged retrieval, independently recovers the last transcript user message and then applies model-derived credit.

The Stop call boundary does not carry retrieval_id, turn_id, episode_id, causal_id or generation into relevance cognition; already-created round identity is therefore dropped and later rediscovered indirectly.

retrieval_episodes schema-enforces retrieval_id primary identity plus unique turn_id, episode_id and causal_id. retrieval_feedback uses receipt_id as primary key but exposes no UNIQUE(retrieval_id, signal_class) cardinality guard.

design_effect.why_no_second_design: The later 10:55:32 packet plus direct schema inspection already generalizes and strengthens every material claim in the 10:54 predecessor. Duplicating the contract would create needless competing nomenclature.
design_effect.preserved_requirement: Carry retrieval_id + turn_id + episode_id + causal_id + generation + exact query/payload identity end-to-end from retrieval admission through noncanonical cognition result and deterministic reduction; session-newest and transcript-latest recovery are DEGRADED compatibility only.
design_effect.cardinality_requirement: If semantics are one model relevance judgement per retrieval, claim/finalization must be transactional and stable-logical-job keyed; value-dependent receipt identity alone is not sufficient exactly-once enforcement.

contradictions_preserved: Strong round identity exists and is schema-enforced upstream, while automatic Stop relevance deliberately uses the weaker session-newest discovery path.
Source topology permits a same-session misbinding scenario, but no wrong-round runtime attachment has been observed in this Triggerword-5 run.
Deterministic receipt hashing occurs only after target selection and therefore cannot repair a previously misselected retrieval row.
The schema does not expose per-retrieval model-feedback cardinality uniqueness; practical double-credit reachability remains a runtime/concurrency question rather than a source-proven occurrence.
counterhypotheses: Installed host hook serialization may keep same-session UserPromptSubmit/Stop ordering strict enough that the source-visible misbinding path is not runtime reachable.
SQLite locking or higher-level ordering may suppress practical competing feedback even though no dedicated model-feedback cardinality constraint is visible.
Transcript-last-user and newest-open retrieval may remain aligned in normal single-flight use despite the weaker binding contract.

required_acceptance: two same-session retrieval rounds with reverse/deferred judgement completion produce zero cross-credit
exact query/payload mutation or transplant is rejected before policy reduction
two competing judgements for one retrieval satisfy the declared one-judgement cardinality without double policy update
stale generation or mismatched retrieval/turn/episode/causal tuple fails closed
transcript-last-user fallback cannot receive exact causal-credit promotion
slow/unavailable cognition cannot prevent deterministic Stop lifecycle bookkeeping
